clinician.final_diagnosis: lead perforation following pacemaker implantation, leading to iatrogenic intercostal artery perforation, a large haemothorax and life-threatening haemorrhagic shock
clinician.trajectory_summary: An early 80s woman had dual chamber pacemaker implantation for bradycardia-tachycardia syndrome. The night after, she developed chest pain with rapid atrial fibrillation and elevated blood pressure. Decreased left breath sounds were noted. Initial labs showed mild troponin elevation and normal hemoglobin. A contrast-enhanced chest CT revealed a large left haemothorax and right ventricular lead perforation. Thoracotomy tube drainage yielded 1.5 L dark blood. Subsequent ECG-gated CT demonstrated active extravasation from the left fourth intercostal artery adjacent to the lead tip causing massive haemothorax and mediastinal shift. Hemoglobin dropped to 103 g/L on transfer. Pacemaker interrogation showed low R wave amplitude and impedance. Imaging depicted extensive haemothorax with lead perforating towards the intercostal artery and thoracic drainage in place. These findings confirm the diagnosis of lead perforation causing iatrogenic intercostal artery injury, massive haemothorax, and clinical deterioration.
